not_examined.what: Concrete token implementations (fee-on-transfer, blacklist, revert-on-zero, rebasing)
not_examined.why: Not present in fixture; token behaviour is assumed generic ERC20 and noted as precondition where it matters

findings.title: Unprotected setPair lets anyone brick borrow and withdrawCollateral (including debt-free users)
findings.mechanism: setPair has no onlyOwner. withdrawCollateral unconditionally calls price() (even when debtOf==0), and price() calls pair.getReserves() and divides by r0. An attacker-controlled pair can revert in getReserves, return r0=0 (division by zero), or return a huge r1/tiny r0 so collateralOf*price overflows; any of these makes withdrawCollateral and borrow revert for every user.
attack_sequence: Attacker deploys a contract whose getReserves() reverts (or returns (0, x))
Attacker calls LendingPool.setPair(malicious)
Every withdrawCollateral/borrow call now reverts; all collateral is frozen
If owner or anyone resets the pair, attacker can call setPair again (or front-run/back-run), so the freeze is effectively sustained
findings.impact: All deposited collateral, including that of users with zero debt, cannot be withdrawn while the malicious pair is set; griefable by anyone at negligible cost and re-applicable at will. (Same root also enables price manipulation/theft - access-control/oracle classes.)
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry: deposit collateral as user A with no debt; from attacker call setPair(RevertingPair); assert A.withdrawCollateral(x) reverts. Repeat with a pair returning (0,1) for division-by-zero.

findings.title: PayoutSplitter.distribute is all-or-nothing push payment; one failing recipient locks all funds permanently
findings.mechanism: distribute loops over the immutable recipient list and requires every token.transfer to succeed. There is no pull-based claim, no way to change recipients, and no rescue function (owner is stored but unused). If any single transfer reverts or returns false - recipient blacklisted by the token (e.g. USDC-style), recipient is address(0) for a token that rejects it, a 0-bps share (or small balance) yields a zero-amount transfer on a revert-on-zero token, or the list is so long that the loop of external transfers exceeds the block gas limit - every distribution reverts.
attack_sequence: Deployer configures recipients (one of them later becomes blacklisted, or is address(0), or has 0 bps on a revert-on-zero token)
Tokens accumulate in the splitter
distribute() reverts on the bad recipient every time
No alternative path exists; the whole balance is permanently stuck
preconditions: A recipient whose transfer fails, or a token that reverts on zero/blacklisted transfers, or a very large recipient list
findings.impact: Permanent loss of access to the entire splitter balance for all recipients.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry: deploy with a mock token that reverts transfers to one recipient (blacklist) or on amount 0 with sharesBps containing 0; fund splitter; assert distribute() reverts and there is no other exit.

findings.title: RewardPool overflow in rewardPerToken permanently freezes withdraw, claim, stake and setRewardRate
findings.mechanism: rewardPerToken computes (block.timestamp - lastUpdate) * rewardRate * 1e18 with checked arithmetic and no cap on rewardRate. Every state-changing path (stake, withdraw, claim, setRewardRate) calls _updatePool first. If the product overflows, all of them revert - including setRewardRate, so the owner cannot lower the rate to recover. withdraw has no emergency path that skips reward accounting, so principal is locked too.
attack_sequence: Owner (by mistake or maliciously/compromised) calls setRewardRate(very large), e.g. > type(uint256).max / 1e18
After >=1 second with totalStaked > 0, rewardPerToken() overflows
withdraw/claim/stake/setRewardRate all revert forever
preconditions: Owner privilege to set an extreme rewardRate
findings.impact: Permanent, irrecoverable lock of all staked principal and rewards. Needs privilege, but is irreversible once set.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry: stake, setRewardRate(type(uint256).max/1e18 + 1), warp 1s; assert withdraw and setRewardRate(0) both revert.

findings.title: RewardPool.claim is all-or-nothing and reverts for late claimants when reward balance is short
findings.mechanism: Rewards are accrued at rewardRate with no check that the contract holds enough rewardToken, and claim transfers the full accrued amount with require. Additionally stake() does not checkpoint the user (no _updateUser), so a fresh staker has userRewardPerTokenPaid=0 and is credited staked*rewardPerToken immediately, which can drain the reward balance. Once the balance is below a user's accrued amount, that user's claim reverts; there is no partial claim.
attack_sequence: Attacker stakes after rewardPerTokenStored has grown (paid stays 0)
Attacker claims an outsized reward, draining rewardToken
Honest users' claim() now reverts because transfer of their full accrued amount fails
preconditions: rewardPerTokenStored > 0 (any time after rewards began), or simply underfunding by owner
findings.impact: Honest stakers cannot claim rewards (stake principal remains withdrawable since withdraw does not pay rewards). Temporary if owner refunds; the root accounting bug is a theft-class issue.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry: user A stakes, warp, attacker stakes fresh and claims; then A.claim() reverts with transfer failure.

findings.title: ShareVault deposits permanently revert (division by zero) once totalAssets reaches 0 with totalSupply > 0
findings.mechanism: previewDeposit divides by totalAssets() whenever totalSupply != 0. withdraw computes shares = assets*totalSupply/totalAssets rounding DOWN, so when share price > 1 a user can withdraw assets while burning 0 shares, repeatedly, until totalAssets()==0 while totalSupply>0 (also reachable if the asset balance is lost/rebased away). From then on every deposit reverts with division by zero and withdraw reverts too; there is no way to reset totalSupply.
attack_sequence: Share price exceeds 1 (e.g. attacker deposits 1 wei and donates, or yield accrues)
Attacker repeatedly calls withdraw(a) with a*totalSupply < totalAssets, burning 0 shares each time
totalAssets() hits 0 while totalSupply > 0
All future deposit() calls revert (division by zero); vault is permanently unusable
preconditions: totalAssets > totalSupply at some point, or external loss of the asset balance
findings.impact: Vault permanently bricked for new deposits; also accompanies theft of existing depositors' assets (rounding-direction bug is primarily arithmetic/theft class).
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry: deposit 1 wei, donate 1e18, loop withdraw(totalAssets()-1 style small amounts burning 0 shares) until totalAssets()==0; assert deposit(1) reverts with panic 0x12.

findings.title: LendingPool collateral withdrawal depends on a live, non-empty pair even for debt-free users
findings.mechanism: Independently of setPair, price() reverts whenever the configured SimplePair has reserve0 == 0: before the pair is seeded/synced, or if sync() truncates a token0 balance that is a multiple of 2^112 to uint112 0. Because withdrawCollateral always calls price(), users with zero debt cannot get their collateral back in that state.
attack_sequence: Pair deployed but not yet seeded/synced (reserve0 == 0), or (impractically) anyone donates token0 so balance == k*2^112 and calls sync()
Any withdrawCollateral reverts with division by zero
findings.impact: Temporary-to-indefinite freeze of all collateral until reserves are non-zero; truncation variant needs ~5.2e33 base units of token0 so is impractical for normal tokens.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry: deploy pool with an unsynced pair, depositCollateral, then withdrawCollateral -> panic 0x12.

cleared.why: Unbounded loop over borrowers (which anyone can grow via repeated borrow(0) after full repay or with zero collateral) is in a view function only; no state-changing path depends on it.
Underflow only when repaying more than own debt; self-inflicted, no third-party DoS.
No dependency on price or pair; only the caller's transferFrom.
Does not transfer rewards, so reward insolvency does not block principal; only blocked by the rewardRate overflow finding.
Divides by totalSupply, which is >0 whenever caller holds shares; reverts only in the bricked state already reported.
Reverts are user-input driven (no input, k check, reserve1 < amountOut); reserve0 can never exceed balance because token0 never leaves the pair, so the subtraction cannot be griefed into underflow.
Bounded by deployer input at deploy time; not a runtime liveness path.

notes: Other classes observed (not in scope): LendingPool.setPair missing access control and spot-price oracle manipulable via SimplePair (oracle/theft); no liquidation in LendingPool (bad debt); RewardPool.stake missing _updateUser checkpoint (reward theft); ShareVault withdraw rounds in withdrawer's favour and first-depositor inflation (arithmetic/theft); SimplePair has no liquidity-removal path so any seeded liquidity is unrecoverable by design, and sync() silently truncates to uint112; PayoutSplitter leaves rounding dust and has an unused owner.
